data.description:
## Problem
`git commit --amend -F <file>` (and `-m`) REPLACES the entire commit message, dropping the
`Change-Id` trailer. Gerrit's `commit-msg` hook then stamps a NEW Change-Id, so the next push
creates a SECOND Gerrit change instead of a new patchset on the existing one. The original change
is left orphaned and must be abandoned by hand.

This happened TWICE in one session (2026-08-19), producing abandoned duplicates Gerrit 1921 and
1926. Both agents recovered — restored the original Change-Id, re-pushed as a new patchset, and
abandoned the duplicate — so the cost is cleanup and reviewer confusion rather than lost work.

## A hook CANNOT fix this — measured, not assumed
`prepare-commit-msg` looked like the natural home (this repo already uses it as a clone-local rail
that blocks commits on `main`, and `--no-verify` does not bypass it). It does not work. Measured
directly in a throwaway repo:

| invocation | hook receives |
|---|---|
| `git commit --amend --no-edit` | `source='commit'  sha='HEAD'` — detectable |
| `git commit --amend -F <file>` | `source='message' sha=''` — **identical to a fresh `-F` commit** |

Git does not tell the hook that an `-F` amend is an amend, so the hook cannot distinguish "amending,
preserve the Change-Id" from "new commit, stamp one". Gerrit's own `commit-msg` hook is no help
either: by design it only ADDS a Change-Id when absent and does nothing when one is present.

Nor does the server catch it. Gerrit rejects the same Change-Id in multiple changes and multiple
Change-Id lines, but a commit carrying a FRESH Change-Id is indistinguishable from a legitimate new
change — which is exactly why both incidents produced silent duplicates rather than a push rejection.

## How the Gerrit ecosystem actually solves it (prior art)
Every large Gerrit project removes the failure mode by ensuring contributors never hand-run
`git commit --amend` + `git push refs/for/*`:

| project | wrapper |
|---|---|
| Go | `git codereview change` — creates a new commit, or amends the existing one PRESERVING the Change-Id |
| OpenStack / OpenDev | `git-review` (`git review`) |
| Android | `repo upload` |
| Chromium | `git cl upload` (depot_tools) |

The documented backstop is a prohibition: OpenStack's contributor guide states plainly not to use
`-m` to supply a commit message, because it overrides the previous message and regenerates the
Change-Id. `-F` behaves identically.

**No major Gerrit project implements a hook or pre-push guard for this.** They make the failure
UNREACHABLE rather than DETECTABLE.

## Scope
Follow the prior art. Add a thin wrapper and make it the documented path.

1. A `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` target (thin script if the Makefile recipe gets unwieldy) that
   amends HEAD with the contents of FILE while CARRYING FORWARD the existing `Change-Id` trailer
   from the current HEAD message. If HEAD has no Change-Id, it must fail loudly rather than
   silently amending — a missing trailer means the commit-msg hook is not installed, which is its
   own problem (`make hooks`).
2. Update `AGENTS.md` line ~280, which currently reads
   "Iterate on findings with `git commit --amend --no-edit` (keep the `Change-Id`) + re-push",
   to also name `make amend-msg FILE=…` as the path for a REWRITTEN message, and to state
   explicitly that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate change.

**EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — do not build:** a `pre-push` hook, a reflog-based Change-Id comparison,
or any other novel guard. A reflog rail was designed and REJECTED for this ticket: no project in the
ecosystem does it, so we would be maintaining a bespoke hook with no prior art to borrow from when
it misfires, to detect a failure the wrapper prevents outright.

## Why this matters more here than upstream
Those projects' contributors are humans using `$EDITOR`, where the pull toward `-m`/`-F` is weak.
rebar's contributors are largely AGENTS composing raw git commands, for whom `-F` is the natural way
to write a multi-line message without shell-quoting pain. The remedy transfers; the incentive to
bypass it is stronger, which is why the wrapper must be the DOCUMENTED DEFAULT rather than merely
available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` amends HEAD with FILE's contents and the resulting commit
      carries the SAME `Change-Id` as before the amend — proven by a test that captures the
      Change-Id before and after and asserts equality.
- [ ] The same test proves the naive form still loses it: `git commit --amend -F <file>` on the
      same fixture yields a DIFFERENT (or absent) Change-Id. Without this contrast the first
      criterion can pass vacuously.
- [ ] `make amend-msg` fails loudly and non-zero when HEAD carries no `Change-Id`, rather than
      producing a commit that will be stamped with a fresh one.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` names `make amend-msg` as the path for a rewritten commit message and states
      that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate Gerrit change.
- [ ] No `pre-push` hook, reflog comparison, or other guard is added.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Provenance
Filed 2026-08-19 after two duplicate changes (Gerrit 1921, 1926) in one session. The hook-based
approach was investigated and empirically disproved before filing; the wrapper approach follows
Go, OpenStack, Android and Chromium practice.
data.title: Add make amend-msg wrapper so amending a commit cannot drop its Change-Id
